segments.t: As soon as Elena Pavlovna mentions that she will run the kitchen completely free of charge, Nagiyev's hesitation vanishes and he happily accepts her offer. He sends a frantic message ahead to the kitchen so Chef Barinov can hide before Elena walks in.
Не волнуйтесь, даже не волнуйтесь, денег не возьму.
Я там это, на кухне, перехвачу.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
Не волнуйтесь, даже не волнуйтесь, денег не возьму.
'Do not worry, do not even worry, I will not charge you a ruble.' Barinov shows a frank approach right away, combining "volnuytes" ("worry") and "deneg" ("money") so the key meaning lands right away.
'Yes, that is very important.' Elena adopts a natural footing toward Nagiyev, putting "vazhno" ("important, mattering") alongside "da" ("yes") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Completely free of charge.' Nagiyev presents a playful style on the spot, combining "sovershenno" ("quite, completely") and "besplatno" ("for free") so the key meaning lands right away.
'Elena Pavlovna.' Barinov takes a brisk footing in their talk, combining "yelena" ("Yelena") and "pavlovna" ("Pavlovna") so the key meaning lands right away.
'What do you think?' Elena wonders decisively without holding back, weaving "kak" ("how") together with "schitayete" ("to count, to think") just the way native speakers do.
'That sounds great.' Nagiyev strikes an emphatic view straight away, anchoring the Russian line on "eto" ("this") and "to" ("that") without extra filler.
'That is what I am saying.' Barinov sustains a measured line right away, pairing "govoryu" ("am telling") with "ya" ("I") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'Give it a try.' Elena sets a grounded tack at once, putting all the weight on "poprobuyte" ("try, taste") so the reply lands immediately.
Я там это, на кухне, перехвачу.
'I will just go check on things in the kitchen first.' Nagiyev offers a wry rhythm for Barinov, leaning on "tam" ("there") before closing the thought with "kukhne" ("kitchen").
'Excuse me, pardon me.' Barinov conveys a pointed rhythm in the room, leaning on "izvinite" ("sorry, excuse me") before closing the thought with "prostite" ("excuse me").
'Viktor Petrovich.' Elena conveys an earnest approach straight away, joining "viktor" ("Viktor") to "petrovich" ("Petrovich") so every word pulls its weight.

'Dmitry Vladimirovich asked me to pass this on.' Barinov strikes a brisk footing straight away, building the phrase around "prosil" ("ask for") and "peredat" ("to pass on") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'Out of the way!' Barinov offers an easygoing manner straight away, leaning on "dorogi" ("roads") as a compact, one-word response that needs no extra words.
Не волнуйтесь, даже не волнуйтесь, денег не возьму.
Я там это, на кухне, перехвачу.
That wraps up this scene as once Elena Pavlovna says she will work completely for free, Nagiyev eagerly accepts and sends a waiter to warn Barinov in the kitchen. See you next time!
